questions.question: What is the purpose of this MR?
questions.answer: It introduces a new invoice status model: a nullable invoices.status column (backfilled from the legacy state column) with two new values, partially_paid and uncollectible, and moves the transition logic and API output to status while still dual-writing the legacy state.

questions.question: What is the main risk in this MR that a reviewer should scrutinize?
questions.answer: The migration backfills every row of the invoices table with a single UPDATE (with a correlated EXISTS on payments) in the same migration transaction as the schema change, which can hold locks and run very long on a large table; it should be batched or run out of band.
must_mention: single UPDATE over the whole invoices table

questions.question: What happens when a payment smaller than the invoice total is applied to an open invoice?
questions.answer: apply_payment records the payment, and since paid_cents is below total_cents and the effective status is open, it transitions the invoice to partially_paid (legacy state stays open). A later payment that reaches the total moves it to paid.
must_mention: later payment reaching total makes it paid

questions.question: Where does the transition logic live, and what is the effective_status property for?
questions.answer: In app/services/invoices.py: the TRANSITIONS table and the transition function. Invoice.effective_status in app/models/invoice.py falls back to the legacy state value when status is still null (rows not yet backfilled or new rows).
must_mention: effective_status falls back to state when status is null

questions.question: What gap or design question should a reviewer raise in the new state machine?
questions.answer: partially_paid has no transition to void, so a partially paid invoice can no longer be voided (the old open to void path is lost for it); also uncollectible and partially_paid invoices both map to legacy state open, and the dual-written state column has no removal plan.
must_mention: dual write of state and status
